note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor after the userns conversion. The unit's only change since the last verdict is userns.Enter(t) as its first statement (the child re-runs the whole body in its own user, network and mount namespace; a child failure or skip propagates to the parent, and a child that ran nothing fails it) plus removal of EPERM/EACCES skips, so a refused privilege now fails instead of skipping. Assertions are byte-identical. Section 3.0: Kind=19, Length=18, and 'The MD5 digest is always 16 bytes in length, and the option would appear in every segment of a connection.' Positive: TestRFC2385CapturedSegmentsHaveIndependentDigests applies assertRFC2385Digest to every captured segment of the full lifecycle in both directions, which requires exactly one Kind 19 option of 18 octets whose 16 digest octets match the oracle. Negative: TestRFC2385MalformedWireSignaturesAreDropped sends SYNs with the option missing, Kind 30, and Length 17, each with valid ordinary checksums, and requires no reply in 300ms followed by a SYNACK to a correctly encoded signed control.
